supporters.quote: We achieved 92% prediction accuracy in the Arizona cohort, 92% prediction accuracy in the ADNI cohort, and 90% prediction accuracy when combining the two demographically distinct cohorts, as compared to 79% (Arizona) and 72% (ADNI) prediction accuracy using hippocampal volume.
supporters.page: 1-2 (abstract); results pp.6-7 (Table 4 comparison, random forest with leave-one-out on the same data sets)
supporters.note: Stonnington et al. 2021, J Alzheimers Dis, author manuscript. Task is prediction of progression from cognitively unimpaired to amnestic MCI within about 2 years (38 Arizona, 120 ADNI; 78 progressors, 80 matched nonprogressors), not MCI detection or MCI-to-dementia conversion. Head-to-head against whole hippocampal volume with the same classifier. Surface features use 5-fold CV with sparse coding while the volume comparison uses leave-one-out, and the surface pipeline adds a learned representation, so the gain is not purely descriptor granularity. Small groups; no amyloid or tau confirmation.

supporters.quote: Notably, the GM FD was the top-ranking predictive feature (Figure 4). The median absolute SHAP value of the GM FD was significantly higher than that of the second-ranking feature, i.e., hippocampal volume (one-tailed Wilcoxon signed rank p-value < 0.001).
supporters.note: Marzi et al. 2023, Front Hum Neurosci, VMCI-Tuscany, 64 MCI with moderate to severe leukoaraiosis, single centre, 18 converters to dementia at 2 years. Evidence is feature importance (SHAP) inside one XGBoost model whose overall AUC is 0.69 (90% CI 0.53-0.85), not a comparison of the discriminative performance of FD-only versus volume-only models. Supports 'cortical fractal dimension outranks hippocampal and cortical GM volume as a predictor of conversion' in vascular MCI; does not establish superior performance. Population is vascular/SVD MCI, not typical AD-spectrum MCI.

supporters.quote: The cortical thickness, which tended to decrease with the disease grade, exhibited in general worse discriminating capabilities than the sulcal features (and the width in particular) ... There were no regions whose CT differed significantly between MCInc and MCIc.
supporters.page: 8 (results, cortical thickness analysis); p.10 discussion ('the classification performances obtained using sulcal width were greater than those resulting from volumetric parameters')
supporters.note: Sighinolfi et al. 2024, J Alzheimers Dis, Bologna, 37 MCI (25 converters, 12 non-converters), 25 AD, 25 HC, 1.5T, single site. The in-paper head-to-head comparator is regional cortical thickness (Desikan-Killiany), not coarse whole-structure volumetry. The volumetry comparison is a one-sentence reference to the authors' earlier study of the same cohort (parahippocampal and fusiform volumes), without numbers here. AUC 0.907 for right S.T.i.post width is the best of 106 sulci x 4 measures, in-sample with leave-one-out giving 2-4% lower values; selection of the best feature per contrast inflates the estimate. Supports 'sulcal width beat regional cortical thickness for MCI conversion' in one small cohort.

supporters.quote: Cortical diffusivity (PerpPD+ in medial-temporal and connected regions) outperformed hippocampal volume, cortical volume, and cortical thickness in Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, predicting faster conversion to dementia.
supporters.page: 1 (abstract); results pp.7-8 (log-rank chi-square 20.19 PerpPD+, 13.01 HVF, 19.46 CT signature, 0.78 CVF; pairwise N+ curves: 'only the PerpPD+ signature curve was significantly different compared to cortical volume fraction')
supporters.note: Torso et al. 2025, Alzheimers Dement, NACC, 826 participants, 196 MCI in the survival analysis, multi-site 3T. Formal pairwise superiority is shown only against whole-cortex volume fraction; the advantage over hippocampal volume and over the cortical-thickness signature is numerical (median survival, chi-square) and not significant in pairwise tests. Dichotomised markers with cut-points from CU vs AD. Authors are employees/co-founder of Oxford Brain Diagnostics, which holds the patent on the diffusion method. Diffusion microstructure rather than T1 morphometry; counted as 'cortical-microstructure diffusion' per the ledger statement.

supporters.quote: When group differences in FA/DA/MD/RD at each ROI ... no significant differences in full tract diffusion tensor metrics between controls and MCI patients that withstood the FDR correction were found ... MCI patients had significantly increased MD and RD in parietal tract segments as compared to controls ... ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 74.97%.
supporters.note: Delvenne et al. 2023, Neurosci Lett, NACC, 20 MCI, 20 AD, 20 controls, single protocol. The comparator is the full-length version of the same parietal splenium bundle, not 'whole-splenium', and no AUC is reported for the full-tract or whole-splenium measure, so there is no performance head-to-head. The segmentation (6 mm around midline) was introduced to reduce tract-length and density confounds, not as a granularity test. Supports 'a midsagittal parietal sub-tract segment showed MCI-control differences that the full tract did not' in a very small sample; says nothing about volumetry.

supporters.quote: In addition, there were more abnormalities detected in our study along the fiber trajectories using pointwise comparison and it is rather sensitive to detect subtle alterations between IPD-NCI and IPD-MCI ... simply averaging over the entire length of fiber tract was not sensitive enough to depict subtle abnormalities at the certain region of WM fiber.
supporters.page: 6 (discussion); results pp.3-4; SVM result p.4 (validation AUC 0.80)
supporters.note: Yu et al. 2023, Parkinsonism Relat Disord, Shenyang, idiopathic Parkinson's disease: 30 PD-MCI, 40 PD-NCI, 30 HC. PD-MCI, not AD-spectrum MCI. The segment-versus-whole-tract contrast is about the number of significant group differences, not classification performance; the SVM (AUC 0.80) used only segmental features plus clinical characteristics and was not compared with a whole-tract-mean model. Comparator is whole-tract diffusion averaging, not volumetry.

supporters.quote: As input data, the model utilizes voxel intensity values from a 3D bounding box surrounding the entire hippocampal region ... the analysis reveals that 10.5% of the volume of the hippocampus was redundant in the differentiation between stable and progressive MCI.
supporters.note: Kwak et al. 2022, Cereb Cortex, ADNI (trained AD vs CN, tested on 118 pMCI, 263 sMCI; accuracy 75.85%, AUC 0.777). The classifier uses whole-hippocampus voxel intensities; subfields enter only through occlusion (attribution) analysis. No subfield-volumetry model is built and nothing is compared against whole hippocampal volume. Shows subfields contribute unevenly to a whole-hippocampus model; does not show that subfield descriptors outperform whole-structure volumetry.

supporters.quote: MCI participants exhibited significant decrease in memory scores and notable volumetric changes in hippocampal subfields, including the bilateral hippocampal tail, subiculum, CA1, CA3, molecular layer, as well as the left presubiculum, parasubiculum, CA4, GC-ML-DG, and HATA.
supporters.note: Singh et al. 2024, Aging and Health Research, CBR-TLSA Bangalore, 36 HC, 27 MCI. Searched for any whole-hippocampus volume comparator or any discrimination metric: none reported. Group differences (GLM, uncorrected across 24 subfields) and correlations with ACE memory only. Cannot support a claim that subfields outperform whole-structure volumetry.

narrowed_wording: In three single-cohort or two-cohort studies, a finer-grained structural descriptor outperformed or outranked a whole-structure volume for predicting progression: hippocampal surface morphometry over hippocampal volume for cognitively unimpaired to amnestic MCI (Arizona, ADNI), cortical minicolumn diffusivity over cortical volume fraction for MCI to dementia (NACC; numerically but not significantly over hippocampal volume), and cortical fractal dimension ranking above hippocampal volume as a SHAP predictor of MCI to dementia in vascular MCI (VMCI-Tuscany). Subfield volumetry, sulcal width and tract-segment diffusion have not been compared head-to-head with whole-structure volumetry in this corpus.
reasoning: Checked against the source documents, only two of eight supporters report a direct performance comparison against coarse whole-structure volumetry: P-177 (surface morphometry 92% vs hippocampal volume 79%/72%) and P-581 (cortical diffusivity versus hippocampal volume and cortical volume fraction, significant pairwise only against cortical volume fraction; industry-authored). P-245 adds a third study with a volumetric comparator, but its evidence is SHAP importance within one modest model (AUC 0.69), so it is partial. P-560 beats regional cortical thickness, not volumetry, and refers to volumetry only via the authors' prior paper. P-408 and P-91 compare segmental against whole-tract diffusion, a different comparator, with no performance head-to-head (P-91 is Parkinson's disease MCI). P-182 and P-899 contain no comparison with whole-hippocampal volume at all: P-182 is an attribution analysis of a whole-hippocampus model and P-899 reports subfield group differences only. The statement as the review states it (the whole list of descriptor types 'outperforms coarse whole-structure volumetry', 8 supporters) therefore overstates the evidence: yes_count is 2. It survives in narrower form because three studies from three distinct datasets and three method families (surface morphometry, cortical diffusion, fractal dimension) show a finer-grained descriptor beating or outranking a whole-structure volume, all for progression prediction rather than cross-sectional MCI detection. The count in Table A1 should fall from 8 and the named descriptor types (subfield volumetry, sulcal width, tract-segment diffusion) should be removed from the claim or listed as untested against volumetry.
